question: *Euthalia malaccana*, which was officially recorded in the Leparada district of Arunachal Pradesh in May 2025, is a new species of which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Butterfly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The species **Euthalia malaccana**, commonly known as the **Fruhstorfer's Baron**, is a rare and beautiful species of **Butterfly**.
 
• It was officially recorded and documented in the **Leparada** district of **Arunachal Pradesh** in **May 2025**, marking a significant addition to the **entomological** records of the state.
 
• The **Euthalia** genus belongs to the **Nymphalidae** family, which is also known as the family of **brush-footed** butterflies because their front legs are usually reduced and hairy.
 
• The discovery of **Euthalia malaccana** in **India** highlights the immense **biodiversity** of the **Eastern Himalayas**, which serves as a critical **habitat** for various **endemic** and rare **Lepidoptera** species.
 
• This specific recording involved **researchers** and **nature enthusiasts** who documented the **physical characteristics** and **wing patterns** of the specimen to distinguish it from other closely related species like the **Common Baron**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh:**

 
 
• Known as the **"Orchid State of India"** or the **"Paradise of the Botanists"**, it is a hotspot for **biodiversity**.
 
• The state is home to over **50%** of the total **butterfly** species found in **India**, including the state butterfly, **Kaiser-i-Hind** (Teinopalpus imperialis).
 
• Geographically, it borders **Bhutan**, **China (Tibet)**, and **Myanmar**, creating a unique **confluence** of various **biogeographic zones**.
 
 
 
• **The Genus Euthalia:**
 
 
• The genus **Euthalia** contains medium to large-sized **butterflies** typically found in **South** and **Southeast Asia**.
 
• These butterflies are often referred to as **Barons**, **Counts**, or **Admirals**, depending on their specific sub-groupings.
 
• They are known for their **cryptic coloration** on the underside of their **wings**, which helps them **camouflage** against **leaf litter** and **forest floors**.
 
 
 
• **Nymphalidae Family:**
 
 
• This is the **largest family** of **butterflies** with about **6,000 species** worldwide.
 
• Members are characterized by a **reduced pair of forelegs** that lack **claws** and are not used for **walking**.
 
• Important examples include the **Monarch**, **Painted Lady**, and the **Common Nawab**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Leparada Recording:**

 
 
• The **Leparada** district, with its **temperate** and **subtropical** climate, provides the perfect **ecosystem** for rare **insects**.
 
• Documenting **Euthalia malaccana** in **2025** adds to the **data** required for **conservation** planning under the **Wildlife Protection Act** of **India**.
 
• Butterflies are considered **indicator species**; their presence or absence provides **data** regarding the **health** of the **environment** and the **impact of climate change** on local **habitats**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Overview:**
 
 
• **Grasshopper:** These are **orthopteran** insects known for **jumping** and **stridulation** (producing sound by rubbing body parts). They are not part of the **Lepidoptera** order.
 
• **Dragonfly:** Belonging to the order **Odonata**, they are **predatory** insects with **multifaceted eyes** and two pairs of strong **transparent wings**.
 
• **Locust:** These are a collection of certain species of **short-horned grasshoppers** in the family **Acrididae** that have a **swarming phase**; they are major **agricultural pests**.
